title: Mon Laferte Will Receive Social Justice Award & More Uplifting Moments in Latin Music
summary: Additionally, Marc Anthony & Yandel will be honored as Agents of Change at Premios Juventud.
body: From career milestones to new releases to major announcements and those little important moments, Billboard editors highlight uplifting moments in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week. Mon Laferte to Receive Social Justice Award This week, it was announced that Mon Laferte will receive the Social Justice Award at the 39th annual Hispanic Heritage Awards, taking place Sept. 10 at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis. The Chilean singer will be honored for using her art, music and platforms to promote conversations about human rights, gender equality and social justice in Latin America and around the world. “I feel incredibly honored. I never imagined that a moment would come in my life or career when my work to carry out the projects that truly matter to me would be recognized,” Laferte said in a statement. “I believe one of the greatest strengths of the Latino community is our ability to build connections, welcome and care for one another, wherever we may be. Knowing that my work can contribute to that sense of community, create a meaningful impact and inspire others is deeply rewarding.” As this year’s honoree, Laferte joins singer…

title: Vera Blue covers Radiohead’s ‘Creep’ for triple j’s Like A Version
summary: Blue also performed "Maze," a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals.
body: Vera Blue has taken on one of alternative rock’s most enduring songs, covering Radiohead ‘s “Creep” for triple j’s Like A Version . The Australian singer-songwriter stripped the 1992 track back to three elements — electric guitar, piano and vocals — building from the lower end of her range into a soaring falsetto by the chorus. Late in the performance she deployed The Pipe, a mouth-controlled dynamic effects processor and synthesizer made by SOMA Laboratory, adding an eerie texture to the arrangement. Blue said she was drawn to the song’s emotional core, describing “Creep” as an “epic rock song” whose lyrics are also “heartbreaking,” and aiming for a “very haunting version” that still nods to Thom Yorke’s original. Blue also performed “Maze,” a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals , during her studio session. The album is due Friday, Aug. 21 via Island Records/Universal Music Australia, and Blue will support it with a national tour opening the same night at Brisbane’s Princess Theatre and running through Perth’s The Rechabite on Aug. 28. Born Celia Pavey, Ve…

title: Brandi Carlile Postpones U.K. and European Tour Citing ‘Personal Circumstances’
summary: The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027.
body: Brandi Carlile has postponed the UK and European leg of her tour, citing “personal circumstances,” the singer-songwriter announced on social media Friday (Aug. 7). The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027. Carlile did not specify the reason beyond describing it as a personal matter. View this post on Instagram “I have been so profoundly anxious about this decision, and I’m aware that this change may be disappointing and inconvenient for many of you, especially those of you who were planning on traveling internationally,” she wrote, adding that she hoped the rescheduling would give fans time to adjust their plans. “I want nothing more than to see my friends across the pond and I have done everything in my power to avoid rescheduling this tour.” The postponement affects several dates. Carlile’s Lisbon show has been canceled outright, while two new dates in Wolverhampton, England, and Copenhagen have been added. Refunds will be issued to Lisbon ticket holders, and fans holding tickets to England shows that have changed venues will be offered full refunds along with priority presale access to the new dat…

title: Angélique Kidjo to Become First African Musician to Receive a Star on Hollywood Walk of Fame
summary: Kidjo’s star ceremony is set for Aug. 18 at 11:30 a.m. PT.
body: Musical icon Angélique Kidjo is set to become the first African musician, and the first Black African performer, to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Related Karol G, David Guetta, Kate Hudson & More Getting Stars on Hollywood Walk of Fame: Full 2026-27 List Chris Blackwell, Angélique Kidjo and Arvo Pärt Named 2023 Polar Music Prize Laureates Charlie Worsham Talks New Album 'Once Upon a Second Time Around,' Collabs With Lainey Wilson, Stephen Wilson Jr. Kidjo joins Charlize Theron , a white South African actress, in representing Africa on the Walk of Fame. The Oscar-winning actress received her star in 2005. Kidjo will receive the 2,854th star. Kidjo’s star ceremony is set for Aug. 18 at 11:30 a.m. PT at 7011 Hollywood Boulevard. Joining Kidjo for the ceremony will be Oscar-nominated actor Willem Dafoe and Grammy- and Primetime Emmy-nominated songwriter/producer Harvey Mason jr. , better known these days as CEO of the Recording Academy and MusiCares. title: In Canada: Osheaga Festival Draws Near-Record Attendance With Tate McRae, Stella Lefty & More

body: Osheaga’s 19th edition was one for the books. The three-day music and arts festival and Montreal just wrapped up its 19th year by logging one of its most successful editions, drawing its second-highest-ever attendance with over 151,000 fans. It’s proof that one of the biggest festivals in Canada continues to get even bigger, with two out of three nights fully sold out this year. title: CORTIS Tells NYC to Put Their Phones Down at First U.S. Solo Concert: The 7 Best Moments
summary: With less than a year on the scene, the five-piece performed like pros at its first full concert in the States for a sold-out show at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden.
body: In under a year since hitting the scene, CORTIS has earned a No. 3 debut on the Billboard 200, a place on Billboard ‘s 21 Under 21 , a Lollapalooza set, a soundtrack single for the Stephen Curry–produced animated film GOAT , a halftime performance at the NBA All-Star Celebrity Game, collaborations with Juicy J and Teezo Touchdown , and are now hitting the U.S. on their first tour. On Thursday (Aug. 6), the quintet consisting of Martin , Juhoon , James , Seonghyeon and Keonho came to the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden for its first-ever solo concert in the States. The show proved CORTIS could live up to that already-stacked résumé while pointing to greater promise of what’s to come next for such promising artists. After kicking off the Put Your Phone Down Tour in July at the Inspire Arena in Incheon, South Korea, CORTIS’ sold-out New York concert split the night in two. The first half ran through nearly all of the group’s discography, with most songs staged with choreography and impactful visuals across tall LED screens in the background.
